rule.description: A merged capability contract couples a function to capability families it does not exercise: either the function consumes a proper subset of the merged contract's families, or it takes on the complete merged contract while exercising none.

checks.description: Detect engine seams and hosts that are forced to accept a complete merged capability contract while exercising only a proper subset of its families.
checks.detected_relation: consumer -> proper subset of merged contract capability families
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The merged contract exceeds the consumer's dependency boundary: the consumer's real dependency is one or two capability families, but its signature and control flow are coupled to every family in the contract.

matches.evidence: fiche-isp: consumer 'fiche_service_boot' uses only the 2 capability families [audit, identity] of merged contract 'Fiche_Provider' but is forced to accept all 4 families; unused: [admission, storage]
fiche-isp: consumer 'start_server' uses only the 1 capability families [audit] of merged contract 'Fiche_Provider' but is forced to accept all 4 families; unused: [admission, identity, storage]

fiche-isp: consumer 'dispatch_connection' uses only the 1 capability families [audit] of merged contract 'Fiche_Provider' but is forced to accept all 4 families; unused: [admission, identity, storage]
fiche-isp: consumer 'handle_connection' uses only the 3 capability families [admission, audit, storage] of merged contract 'Fiche_Provider' but is forced to accept all 4 families; unused: [identity]

checks.description: Detect hosts and entries that must assemble or carry a complete merged capability contract although they exercise no capability family through it.
checks.detected_relation: implementor -> complete merged contract with zero exercised families
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The interface forces the implementor side to depend on capabilities it does not need at all: constructing, storing or accepting the whole merged contract is mandatory even when only default behavior is wanted.

matches.evidence: fiche-isp: implementation 'fiche_run' is forced to carry the complete merged contract 'Fiche_Provider' with 4 capability families while exercising no capability family through it
fiche-isp: implementation 'main' is forced to carry the complete merged contract 'Fiche_Provider' with 4 capability families while exercising no capability family through it

excluded.reason: flat configuration record with no function-pointer capability families; never a merged contract under the rule

excluded.candidate: capability-family payload implementations (printing, log entry, slug/directory/persistence, identity, admission)
excluded.reason: payload implementations behind the seams; they neither consume nor are forced to carry the merged contract
it stores into all four family slots of the merged contract in one place, so no family group is unused there; the forcing is on its callers, which are the reported implementor entries
